DEVELOPMENT.md

Source: DEVELOPMENT.md

Guidance for AI coding agents (and people) extending or modifying evomod2. For using the package, see AGENTS.md; the conventions listed there (standard deviations, per-allele rates, genome layout, optimum carry-over) apply to new code too.

Layout

  • src/evomod.h: the C++ component interfaces (Architecture, Mutation, Fitness, Recombination) and their implementations; src/components.cpp builds components from the R lists (make_*() factories); src/simulate.cpp has the generation loop (evolve_cpp) and C++ helpers exported to R.
  • R/: constructors (architecture.R, model.R, regimes.R, recombination.R), evolve.R, accessors and analysis (accessors.R, statistics.R), plot.R.
  • tests/testthat/: unit tests; validation/: cross-checks against independent implementations (EvoMod.jl, the original C code), not run in CI.
  • inst/examples/: command-line experiments; inst/extdata/: stored summaries used by the results vignettes; vignettes/; _pkgdown.yml and docs/ (the website).

The generation loop

evolve_cpp() in src/simulate.cpp runs the regimes. In every generation, in this order:

  1. the optimum moves (directional(): theta += delta_theta; fluctuating(): a jump after every every generations);
  2. fitness is computed from the current phenotypes (all ones under drift);
  3. reproduction:
    • Wright-Fisher: every genome mutates (Mutation::mutate), n sires and n dames are drawn with probability proportional to fitness, and Recombination::offspring builds the offspring into a separate buffer, which is then swapped in (parents are never overwritten);
    • Moran: n events; each replaces a random individual by an offspring of two parents drawn from a Fenwick tree of fitnesses, the offspring then mutates, and only its fitness is updated;
  4. genotypic values (Architecture::genotypic_value) and phenotypes (x + Normal(0, env_sd)) are computed;
  5. statistics are recorded when generation % record_every == 0.

The optimum carries over between regimes; a regime resets it only when the user gives theta (reset_theta).

Interfaces in detail

  • Architecture: genotypic_value(genome) (traits vector), local_effects(genome) (traits x loci: the change in genotypic value when a locus is set to the reference genotype, all zeros), and optionally allele_effects(genome) (traits x alleles) when genotypic values are sums of allele effects; return an empty matrix otherwise. allele_effects enables the exact g_decomposition() and the recorded genic part of G.
  • Mutation: mutate(genome) (one generation of mutation, using binomial numbers of events), mutate_one(genome) (exactly one event, at a site chosen in proportion to the rates; used by mutational_covariance()), and expected_mutations(genome) (events per genome per generation). Support persistence (new = persistence * old + draw) and keep the += path when it is 1.
  • Recombination: offspring(sire, dame, kid); column 2l of the kid gets one of the sire’s alleles at locus l (0-based), column 2l + 1 one of the dam’s.
  • Fitness: log_fitness(Z) for a traits x individuals matrix.

Random numbers

Use only R’s generator from C++ (R::unif_rand(), R::norm_rand(), R::rbinom(), rnorm_vec()), never <random> or Armadillo’s generator, so that set.seed() and seed = reproduce runs and a population continued over several evolve() calls matches a single call. Draw the random numbers in the same order on every code path you do not mean to change.

Adding a regime or a statistic

  • A regime is an R constructor in R/regimes.R returning a new_regime() list; resolve_regimes() turns it into the list evolve_cpp() reads (generations, selective, reset_theta, theta, delta_theta, omega, and regime-specific fields). Add the per-generation behaviour to the loop in evolve_cpp().
  • A statistic recorded during the run goes into Records in src/simulate.cpp (and into append_records() in R/evolve.R so that continued runs keep it), with an accessor in R/accessors.R. Statistics of the current population that are expensive or optional (shuffles, mutational covariance, additive covariance) are better computed on demand from genomes(pop) in R or through a C++ helper.

Adding a component

Follow the README section “Extending evomod2”: derive a class in src/evomod.h, implement it in src/components.cpp, add a case to the matching make_*() factory, write the R constructor returning a list with a type (architectures also need loci, traits, state_rows, mutation_type), and test it against an explicit, slow R version of the same computation. New models are usually prototyped and cross-checked in EvoMod.jl first.

Build, test, document

Rscript -e 'Rcpp::compileAttributes(); roxygen2::roxygenise()'   # after changing exports or docs
R CMD INSTALL --preclean .
Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'
R CMD build . && R CMD check --no-manual evomod2_*.tar.gz
Rscript -e 'pkgdown::build_site()'                               # website into docs/
  • Time code only from clean builds. devtools::test() and load_all() compile without optimisation and leave the objects in src/; a later R CMD INSTALL . without --preclean reuses them and runs about three times slower. Remove src/*.o and src/*.so after testing.
  • Keep existing behaviour bit-for-bit when adding options with defaults (seeded runs before and after the change must be identical); compilers may fuse multiply-adds, so keep the old arithmetic on the default path.
  • Statistical tests: use enough replicates and tolerances that they do not fail by chance, and prefer exact expectations (identities, analytical equilibria) where they exist.
  • Documentation is roxygen2 (markdown); do not edit man/ or NAMESPACE by hand.
  • Vignettes that run simulations must build in under a minute; heavy results go in inst/extdata/ with the script that produces them in inst/examples/.

Validation, CI and the website

  • validation/cross_check.R (against EvoMod.jl, additive and multilinear) and validation/cross_check_c.R (against the original C code, binary B) compare replicate means of G and trait means; run them after changes to the generation loop, mutation or the architectures they cover.
  • GitHub Actions runs R CMD check on macOS, Ubuntu and Windows for every push to main and every pull request.
  • The website is built by pkgdown into docs/ and served by GitHub Pages from main; rebuild it (pkgdown::build_site()) when documentation or vignettes change. Add new vignettes to _pkgdown.yml.
